bg-28-01.hint: It is a great pleasure to meet you.
bg-28-01.why: Formal statement ending -습니다 attaches to consonant stem 반갑다: 반갑- + -습니다 = 반갑습니다.

bg-28-01.q: Formally announce that you will start the presentation using 지금 발표 and 시작하겠습니다.
bg-28-01.why: The formal future statement ending -겠- + -습니다 creates a professional announcement: 시작하겠습니다.

steps.en: Now I will begin the presentation.
I will now begin today's prepared presentation.

ko: 저는 한국 대학교에서 경영학을 공부하는 학생입니다.
en: Hello. I am Kim Min-soo, in charge of today's presentation.
I am a student studying business administration at Hankuk University.
From now, I will begin the prepared project presentation.

bg-28-01.q: Who is introducing themselves in the presentation?
bg-28-01.why: The speaker says '오늘 발표를 맡은 김민수입니다'.

bg-28-01.q: What does the speaker major in at university?
bg-28-01.why: The text states '경영학을 공부하는 학생입니다' (student studying business administration).

items: Introduce yourself and greet others in formal Korean using -ㅂ/습니다
Ask formal questions in professional settings using -ㅂ/습니까?

bg-28-02.why: Public transit announcements use formal register: 닫히다 + -ㅂ니다 = 닫힙니다.

bg-28-02.q: Formally instruct passengers to step back using 뒤로 and 물러서 주십시오.
bg-28-02.why: Formal public imperative uses -(으)십시오: 물러서 주십시오.

steps.en: Please step back behind the safety door.

ko: 곧 열차가 도착하오니 안전선 뒤로 물러서 주십시오.
출입문이 닫힐 때는 무리하게 타지 마십시오.
en: An announcement chimes at the subway platform.
The train will arrive shortly, so please step back behind the safety line.
When the doors are closing, please do not board forcefully.

bg-28-02.q: Where is the announcement taking place?
bg-28-02.why: The text begins '지하철 승강장에서 안내 방송이 울립니다'.

bg-28-02.q: What instruction is given regarding the closing doors?
options: Hold the door open for friends
bg-28-02.why: The text says '출입문이 닫힐 때는 무리하게 타지 마십시오' (please do not board forcefully).

items: Understand public formal directives ending in -(으)십시오 and -지 마십시오
Convert conversational commands (-세요) into formal announcements

bg-28-03.hint: I live in Seoul right now.
bg-28-03.why: Stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ before -ㅂ니다: 살다 becomes 삽니다.

bg-28-03.q: State formally that you make Korean food using 한국 요리 and 만듭니다.
bg-28-03.why: 만들다 drops ㄹ before -ㅂ니다 to become 만듭니다.

bg-28-03.hint: For ㄹ-stem verbs like 알다, the ㄹ drops before -ㅂ니다: 알다 → 압니다 (never 알습니다).
bg-28-03.why: ㄹ-stem verbs drop ㄹ before -ㅂ니다: 알다 becomes 압니다.

steps.en: I live in Seoul right now.
As for me, I live in Seoul right now.

ko: 저는 한국에 온 지 1년이 되었고 지금 서울에 삽니다.
매일 아침 라디오 뉴스를 들으면서 한국어를 배웁니다.
주말에는 친구들을 위해 맛있는 불고기를 직접 만듭니다.
en: It has been a year since I came to Korea, and I live in Seoul now.
Every morning, I learn Korean while listening to radio news.
On weekends, I make delicious bulgogi myself for my friends.

bg-28-03.q: Where does the speaker live now?
bg-28-03.why: The text says '지금 서울에 삽니다' (I live in Seoul now).

bg-28-03.q: What does the speaker make on weekends for their friends?
bg-28-03.why: The text says '친구들을 위해 맛있는 불고기를 직접 만듭니다'.

items: Conjugate ㄹ-irregular verbs correctly into formal -ㅂ니다 without keeping the ㄹ
Distinguish regular consonant verbs from ㄹ-stem verbs in the formal register

bg-28-04.why: Formal register -겠습니다 expresses polite resolve in interviews and presentations.

bg-28-04.q: Express a formal polite greeting at a business introduction using 처음 뵙겠습니다 and 잘 부탁드립니다.
bg-28-04.why: These two formal fixed expressions are essential for professional introductions.

bg-28-04.hint: In a formal job interview, use the formal register -겠습니다 instead of conversational 해요체.
bg-28-04.why: Interviews demand the formal professional register: 열심히 일하겠습니다.

a.d: Used in official public situations: news broadcasts, presentations, job interviews, subway announcements, and military or business meetings.
ex: 처음 뵙겠습니다. 만나서 **반갑습니다**. — Pleased to meet you for the first time.
지금부터 발표를 **시작하겠습니다**. — I will begin the presentation now.

b.d: Standard polite style for everyday social interactions: talking with colleagues, friends, service staff, or classmates.
ex: 오늘 날씨가 정말 **좋아요**. — The weather is really nice today.
점심에 같이 밥 **먹어요**. — Let's eat lunch together.

bg-28-04.tip: Both styles are equally polite! Use -ㅂ/습니다 when presenting to an audience or speaking on behalf of an organization; use -아/어요 for warm personal conversations.

steps.en: I will work hard at the company.
In my assigned tasks, I will work hard at the company.

ko: 안녕하십니까? 이번 신입 사원 면접에 지원한 이수진입니다.
저는 대학에서 컴퓨터 공학을 전공하였고 팀 프로젝트를 성공적으로 마쳤습니다.
회사에 입사하게 된다면 열정을 가지고 최선을 다해 일하겠습니다.
en: Hello. I am Lee Su-jin, an applicant for this new employee interview.
I majored in computer engineering in college and completed team projects successfully.
If I get to enter this company, I will work hard with passion and do my best.

bg-28-04.q: What is the speaker doing in the passage?
options: Introducing herself in a job interview
Calling a friend to make dinner plans
bg-28-04.why: The text says '이번 신입 사원 면접에 지원한 이수진입니다' (applicant for this new employee interview).

bg-28-04.q: What did Lee Su-jin major in during college?
bg-28-04.why: The text states '대학에서 컴퓨터 공학을 전공하였고'.

items: Choose accurately between formal (-ㅂ/습니다) and polite conversational (-아/어요)
Deliver professional greetings, interview responses, and presentation openings
